name: Trade war & tariffs
summary: China's rare-earth control pause ends 10 Nov with no renewal announced
state: China's one-year suspension of its October 2025 rare-earth export controls, including the 0.1% content rule, expires on 10 Nov, and no renewal had been announced as of 4 Nov; its April 2025 licensing rules remain in force. US tariffs are steady and no new tariff round was announced between 1 and 4 Nov.
for_you: Renewed rare-earth curbs would mostly affect manufacturers of magnets, vehicles and electronics; consumer price effects would lag.
rubric_hit: Major export controls threatened between large economies = Watch

sources.title: FXStreet — China's rare earth leverage has an expiration date: November 10

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
